page: Vultr vhp-4c-12gb-intel is a virtual server belonging to the High Performance family. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and is allocated on a shared basis. The system is equipped with 12.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 260 GB NVMe SSD for local storage.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1466.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1206.0. However, due to the shared CPU allocation, multi-core performance scales poorly, resulting in a weak stress-ng multi-core score of 5747.52 and a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 3843.0. Memory performance is mixed; cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 421.33 GB/sec, but uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to a weak 36.96 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations also fall into the lower performance tiers, as shown by a weak Passmark database operations score of 1351.82.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads requiring a moderate amount of NVMe storage and memory without demanding sustained, dedicated multi-core CPU performance. The shared CPU architecture introduces resource contention risks, making it less suitable for intensive multi-threaded tasks, large database operations, or real-time LLM inference. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as light web serving, software compilation tasks, text processing, and basic Redis caching.
